You are editing a SQL object definition. If this is a table's CREATE and the change alters an
existing column, adds or drops a constraint, or drops the table, it is a schema change that goes
through the ssdt-agent workflow (see `.github/copilot-instructions.md`), authored as an edit to
the CREATE — never as a hand-written ALTER.

Two behaviors surprise SQL-experienced developers who are new to SSDT:

- On a table that holds rows, making a column NOT NULL or narrowing it is blocked by the
  deployment, even after you clear every offending value — the guard fires on whether the table
  holds rows at all, not on the values. The remedy is a two-release change. See
  `ssdt-agent/skills/op/make-mandatory/SKILL.md`.
- Renaming or dropping an object by editing the file, with no refactorlog entry, does not rename
  or drop anything in production. It strands the original and creates an empty new one. See
  `ssdt-agent/skills/_index/identity-and-refactorlog/SKILL.md`.

Find the operation that matches in `ssdt-agent/skills/INDEX.md` and follow its skill. Prove
the change on a disposable copy before you classify it.
